==English==
{{wikidata lexeme|L9593}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂-}}
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:accompanien<ety:bor<fro:acompagner<ety:af<a-><compaing><-er>>>>|tree=+}}
* First attested in early 15th century.
From {{inh|en|enm|accompanien}}, from {{der|en|fro|acompagner||to associate with}}, from {{m|fro|compaing||companion}}, nominative singular of {{m|fro|compaignon||companion}}. See [[company]].

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈkʌm.pə.ni/|/əˈkʌmp.ni/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-accompany.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|ac|com|pa|ny}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To go with or attend as a companion or associate; to keep company with; to go along with.
#: {{ux|en|Geoffrey '''accompanied''' the group on their pilgrimage.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1804|author=[[w:Richard Glover (poet)|Richard Glover]]
|passage=The Persian dames, […] / In sumptuous cars, '''accompanied''' his march.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1581|author=w:Philip Sidney|title=An Apology of Poetry, or a Defense of Poesy|section=Book I
|passage=They are never alone that are '''accompanied''' with noble thoughts.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To supplement with; add to.
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=5|passage=He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights, {{...}}, the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that '''accompanied''' his thoughts.}}
# {{senseid|en|to perform an accompanying part next to another instrument}}{{lb|en|intransitive|music}} To perform an accompanying part or parts in a [[composition]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|music}} To perform an accompanying part next to (another instrument or musician).
#: {{ux|en|The strings were '''accompanied''' by two woodwinds.}}
#: {{ux|en|I will '''accompany''' her on the oboe.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To associate in a company; to keep company.
#* {{RQ:Pliny Holland Historie of the World
|passage=Men say that they will drive away one another, {{...}} and not '''accompanied''' together.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[cohabit]] (with). {{rfex|en}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To cohabit with; to coexist with; occur with.
# To be found at the same time.
#: {{ux|en|Thunder almost always '''accompanies''' lightning during a rain storm.}}

====Usage notes====
{{sense|to go with}} Traditionally, persons were said to be accompanied '''by''', and inanimate objects, states or conditions were said to be accompanied '''with'''. However, this distinction is not generally observed today, and '''by''' is becoming predominant.

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|go with}} {{l|en|attend}}, {{l|en|escort}}, go with
:* We '''accompany''' those with whom we go as companions. The word imports an ''equality'' of station.
:* We '''attend''' those whom we wait upon or follow. The word conveys an idea of ''subordination''.
:* We '''escort''' those whom we attend with a view to ''guard and protect''.
:*: A gentleman '''accompanies''' a friend to some public place; he '''attends''' or '''escorts''' a lady.

====Derived terms====
{{col4|en
|accompaniment|accompanable|accompaniable|accompanier|accompanyist|reaccompany
|accompanist
}}
